paragraphs.title: Taking Refuge in the Most High and Declaring Trust

answers: In the secret place of the most High
In the dwelling of the wicked
easy.explanation: The first verse says that he dwells in the secret place of the most High.
easy.q: Where does the person described at the beginning of the psalm dwell?

easy.explanation: The speaker calls the LORD his refuge and fortress.
easy.q: What does the LORD provide for the person in verse 2?

easy.explanation: He declares, “my God; in him will I trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker say that he will trust?

answers: Because he takes refuge with God, he declares that God is his refuge
Because he turns away from God, he becomes afraid
Because he sees God as his enemy
medium.explanation: The passage moves from dwelling safely with God to openly declaring trust in Him.
medium.q: What connection is shown between dwelling in the secret place and the speaker’s words?

medium.explanation: A fortress is a strong place of defense and protection.
medium.q: What does the word “fortress” mean in the phrase “He is my refuge and my fortress”?

answers: Shelter, declaration of trust, and confidence in God
medium.explanation: The person first dwells in God’s shelter, then declares that God is his refuge and that he trusts Him.
medium.q: Which sequence best represents the ideas in the first two verses?

answers: Inner refuge is expressed through an open declaration
The person leaves his place of safety
challenge.explanation: The verses connect a condition of dwelling safely with a public confession of trust.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from “dwelleth” to “I will say”?

challenge.explanation: Being under the Almighty’s shadow pictures protection as a place in which the person remains.
challenge.q: Which phrase presents the LORD as a place of protection, not merely as one who protects?

answers: That the protection is general rather than personal
That the relationship with God is personal and direct
That the speaker does not know God
challenge.explanation: The repeated “my” shows the speaker’s personal relationship with the LORD.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated personal pronouns in “my refuge,” “my fortress,” and “my God”?

paragraphs.title: Protection from Calamity and the Fears of Night and Day

answers: The snare of the fowler and the noisome pestilence
easy.explanation: Verse 3 names the snare of the fowler and the noisome pestilence.
easy.q: From what does the LORD deliver the person according to verse 3?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night.”
easy.q: What is the person told not to fear?

answers: They fall around the protected person
easy.explanation: The verse says, “A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand.”
easy.q: What happens to the thousand and the ten thousand in verse 7?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions terror by night and an arrow that flies by day.
medium.q: What contrast of time appears in the description of danger?

answers: A deadly disease or destructive plague
medium.explanation: Pestilence refers to a dangerous, widespread disease or plague.
medium.q: What does “pestilence” mean in this passage?

answers: That the person cannot see what is happening
That the danger does not approach the protected person
That the person falls with everyone else
medium.explanation: Even though many fall nearby, the passage says that the destruction will not come near him.
medium.q: What is emphasized by the statement that many fall but the danger “shall not come nigh thee”?

challenge.explanation: The verses mention a snare, pestilence, arrows, destruction, and the falling of many people.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the variety of dangers in this section?

answers: It describes a close and sheltering place of protection
challenge.explanation: Being covered with feathers and trusting under wings pictures intimate shelter and safety.
challenge.q: What role does the image of feathers and wings play in the idea of protection?

answers: The protected person will witness the consequences of wickedness around him
The person is forbidden to look around him
The person falls together with the wicked
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the person as an observer of the wicked’s reward while remaining protected.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked”?

paragraphs.title: Complete Shelter, Angelic Guardianship, and Triumph over Danger

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that the person has made the LORD, the most High, his habitation.
easy.q: Whom has the person made his habitation?

easy.explanation: The LORD gives His angels charge to keep the person in all his ways.
easy.q: Who is commanded to keep the person?

easy.explanation: The passage names the lion, adder, young lion, and dragon.
easy.q: From what kinds of creatures is the person protected in the final verse of the section?

answers: The habitation leads to separation from God
The habitation represents a place of refuge from which protection proceeds
The habitation is a place of danger
medium.explanation: The psalm returns to the idea of dwelling with the Most High and then describes His protection.
medium.q: What is the connection between making the LORD one’s habitation and the promise of protection?

medium.explanation: An adder is a venomous snake, fitting the verse’s list of dangerous creatures.
medium.q: What does the word “adder” refer to in “Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder”?

answers: To keep the person in all his ways and bear him up
To drive the person away from shelter
medium.explanation: The angels are commanded to keep him and to bear him up in their hands.
medium.q: What is the role of the angels in these verses?

answers: The passage moves from refuge with the Most High to angelic protection and victory over dangers
The passage moves from rescue to greater fear
The passage moves from war to celebration
challenge.explanation: The section begins with habitation in the Most High, continues with angelic guardianship, and ends with victory over dangerous creatures.
challenge.q: What change of ideas takes place in verses 9–13?

answers: The protection includes preventing injury along the way
The person must carry the angels
The person loses his place of refuge
challenge.explanation: The angels bear him up so that he will not dash his foot against a stone.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “They shall bear thee up in their hands”?

answers: It shows the person surrendering to danger
It shows the person overcoming dangerous creatures
It shows the creatures protecting the person
challenge.explanation: Treading and trampling portray mastery over the creatures that could threaten him.
challenge.q: How does “Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder” relate to overcoming danger?

paragraphs.title: God’s Response and the Promise of Salvation

answers: Because he has set his love upon Him
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him.”
easy.q: Why will the LORD deliver the person according to verse 14?

easy.explanation: The LORD promises, “He shall call upon me, and I will answer him.”
easy.q: What does God promise to do when the person calls upon Him?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “With long life will I satisfy him.”
easy.q: With what will the LORD satisfy the person?

answers: He desires and clings to God
medium.explanation: The phrase describes devoted love and attachment to the LORD.
medium.q: What does “he hath set his love upon me” mean in this context?

answers: He will answer, be with the person in trouble, deliver, and honor him
He will withdraw, hide, remain silent, and punish
He will send animals, cause the person to fall, hide, and weaken him
medium.explanation: God promises to answer, remain with him in trouble, deliver him, and honor him.
medium.q: Which sequence of God’s responses appears in these verses?

answers: Knowing God’s name is presented as a reason for protection and deliverance
Knowing God’s name causes the person to turn away
There is no connection between them
medium.explanation: God says He will set the person on high because he has known His name, followed by promises of help and salvation.
medium.q: What is the connection between knowing God’s name and the promises given to the person?

answers: The passage becomes a response spoken in God’s name and describes His promises
The speaker returns to describing animals
The speaker stops discussing the person
challenge.explanation: The closing verses present God’s own declarations about what He will do for the person.
challenge.q: What changes in the voice of the speaker in verses 14–16?

answers: “I will answer him” — “I will deliver him”
“He hath set his love” — “He hath known my name”
challenge.explanation: God promises both to answer the person and to deliver him from trouble.
challenge.q: Which pair expresses both God’s presence in trouble and His rescue from it?

answers: Answering, presence in trouble, deliverance, honor, salvation, and long life
challenge.explanation: The final verses promise God’s answer, presence, deliverance, honor, salvation, and satisfaction with long life.
challenge.q: Which group of promises brings the psalm to its conclusion?
